500-day workflow model

Manual and automated workflow costs

The model applies the same workload to manual and automated processes, then compares handling time, follow-up work, labor cost, and backlog.

Two processes under the same workload

Both processes use the team size, task volume, handling time, follow-up rate, and hourly cost entered below. The differences are model estimates, not observed operational results.

Automated Workflow currently saves 0 hours and $0 in labor cost across this 500-day scenario.

Number of people handling the same recurring workflow. A larger team increases both manual workflow cost and the upside from automated workflow.
How many workflow tasks each person completes per day. Higher volume raises total time cost and makes automated workflow ROI easier to see.
Average manual workflow handling time for one task. Automated Workflow reduces this base time cost directly.
Share of tasks that create extra follow-up work, corrections, or manual checks. Automated Workflow lowers this hidden time cost.
$
Blended employer cost for one working hour. The simulator uses it to convert saved time into labor cost impact across the full 500-day run.

This educational model illustrates how assumptions about workload and automation affect estimated time and cost.
